issues: The passage specifies no location or writing materials; keep these visually unspecified.
The people are commanded to write, then the words are expounded after they have been written; do not depict writing and exposition as simultaneous.
The group in scene_002 is unnamed in the verses; “Those commanded to write” is a descriptive label, not an established identity.
The dialogue is an exact contiguous excerpt, but its speaker is Jesus Christ quoting words attributed to the Father; labeling the speaker only “Jesus Christ” omits that attribution.
The one described as coming and appearing is not identified by name in verses 2–3; keep the identity unspecified rather than presenting a named figure as established.
The supplied dialogue and narration are exact excerpts, but the dialogue is part of the prophecy Jesus Christ is reciting; the speaker label should identify that context.
The offering and its participants are future prophetic content, not a narrated present event; the optional symbolic depiction should not imply a specific rite or historical occurrence.
The form and setting of the offering are unspecified.
The listed wrongdoing and judgment are in a prophetic warning, not a narrated present-tense event; visual symbolism should not become a specific incident or identify individuals.
The character label “God” is less precise than the source’s “Lord” and “Lord of Hosts”; the words themselves are correctly attributed in the dialogue.
The Lord of Hosts is named as the speaker of verse 17, but the passage does not describe his visible appearance; depict no appearance or use text-only quotation.
The promise and jewel imagery concern a future day and must not be staged as present events.
